rationale: All 3 prior findings resolved. CR-001 (critical, trailing-newline false negative): command substitution replaced with `git show :f > tmpdir/orig` + `cmp -s tmpdir/orig tmpdir/fixed` — comparison is now byte-exact and preserves trailing newlines; regression test test_missing_trailing_newline_exits_one asserts exit 1 for a staged file written via write_bytes(b'x = 1') without trailing newline. CR-002 (major, syntax-error UX): explicit `if ! $RUFF_CMD format ...; then echo '[pre-commit] Ruff format failed on staged content of \'$f\' (syntax error?):'; cat tmpdir/format.err >&2; exit 1; fi` — helper now surfaces a clear message before exit; regression test test_syntax_error_in_staged_file_reports_clearly asserts the message and file name. CR-003 (major, swallowed ruff failure): ruff check now runs with `rc=0; ... || rc=$?; if [[ $rc -gt 1 ]]; then ... exit 1; fi`; exit 0 (clean) and 1 (fixes/lint remain — the pre_commit.sh read-only `ruff check` step surfaces the latter) are accepted, exit ≥2 is fatal with stderr printed; no regression test added because deliberately breaking RUFF_CMD is trivial by inspection and adding fault-injection scaffolding would exceed scope. Scoped confirmation pass on the fix-up diff refuted the suspicion of new high-risk issues: mktemp+trap are correctly scoped to this subprocess, stderr redirects to tmp files that are cleaned up on EXIT, and the subprocess boundary keeps _ruff_staged.sh's trap from clobbering pre_commit.sh's ERR trap. All 7 tests (5 original + 2 regression) pass locally.
